chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Meeting the young Billie Holiday in 1930
summary: Dave Tough took him to see a vivacious young Billie singing to the tables in a gingham gown.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: This girl... Now I met her when she was a beautiful girl.
Yeah. May Bonds(?)... One time, when Dave Tough came from Paris and worked Ceriuti's, he said, "Come on, I want you to meet this girl." And this is back in 1930...

Ceriuti's was a place on Madison Avenue that hired colored entertainers. A beautiful place. Good artists worked there. So he said, "I want you to see this girl. She's something." So he took me to a place named

Coban's(?) on 132nd Street. This girl, she had a gingham gown on her, and she was vivacious and young and nice, and she was singing to the tables. That's the image I had of her, you know. I was sort of naive in a lot of this. And she said, "How are you doing? Sit down." Oh, she was so vivacious and... She was like sunshine, you know. So I didn't know her... I didn't know what my lowers and uppers were at that time, you know!

Later on, as times went by and the years... This was the early Thirties. She became... Later on, these things began to happen and her lifestyle changed. I think she always felt embarrassed about that. It's just like when you go to school with somebody and they become a big-shot in another way, but it's not the way you knew him in school, and you appear on the scene -- it's that they don't want to see you. When they say, "Lady Day" and all, I say, "What is this...!" But I managed to say Lady Day the way I saw them. It wasn't the image that I had of her. My image was a little more tragic.
